source.title: AdaX: Adaptive Gradient Descent with Exponential Long Term Memory
source.authors: Wenjie Li; Zhaoyang Zhang; Xin-Jiang Wang; Ping Luo

record.file_problem: Text appears complete; no apparent truncation or garbling affecting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: Compares adaptive optimizers with momentum SGD on held-out task metrics, using standard training experiments rather than the claim's random-label setup.
record.gate_note: The synthetic optimization example and second-moment measurements do not measure the generalization gap described in the claim. Hyperparameter search results are tuning choices, not outcome rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares adaptive optimizers with momentum SGD on held-out image-classification performance. It bears on V4, although tuning includes momentum parameters and weight decay, exceeding V4's limited-tuning protocol. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that AdaX is more stable and performs better than Adam on their tested tasks, and can converge faster than SGDM while matching its performance in some settings. This is not universal: AdaX-W remains below SGDM on ResNet-50 ImageNet. They explicitly call for further evaluation.
record.recipe_differences: Compares AdaX and adaptive optimizer variants with SGDM on image classification, language modeling and transfer learning; does not use random-label experiments or measure generalization gaps directly.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and task; model; weight decay method (L2 versus decoupled); AdaX learning rate and momentum settings. The text says larger epsilon improved AdamW on CIFAR-10 by around 0.35 percent accuracy, while AdaX-W was not affected; AdaX-W step sizes and beta settings were also varied.

fits_no_version.finding: On VOC2012 segmentation, AdamW and AMSGrad(W) obtain lower IoU than SGDM: 74.62 and 73.62 versus 76.28.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive optimizers can underperform momentum SGD in semantic-segmentation transfer learning.

fits_no_version.finding: On One Billion Word, AdaX, Adam, and AMSGrad reach perplexities of 35.22, 36.90, and 61.66; no SGD result is provided.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive optimizers differ substantially in language-model performance.

record.problems: The experiments compare held-out performance but do not report training-test gaps for the table results. SGDM is omitted from the language-model comparison as unsuitable for sparse gradients. Several auxiliary outcomes are shown only in figures without exact values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No results-bearing optimizer comparisons from the main results tables were left out. Figure 5 accuracy curves are figure-only; they are recorded without inferred values in R20–R21.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

The exact learning-rate/schedule-only tuning protocol; switching from Adam to SGD; language-model comparisons with SGD; whether broader tuning removes or reverses the deficit; whether decoupled decay fully recovers SGD performance.
Batch-size interventions and adaptation of large-batch recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons with other measures.
Removal of memorized examples and retraining.

missing.what: AMSGrad has substantially higher training accuracy than SGDM on ImageNet ResNet-18 despite worse held-out accuracy. Add the qualitative training comparison supporting V4's training-performance clause.
missing.locator: Section 5.1, Image Classification on ImageNet; Figure 1(c–d)

missing.what: Increasing AdamW epsilon across 1e-8, 1e-5, and 1e-3 improves CIFAR-10 accuracy by approximately 0.35 percentage points.

record.verdict_notes: The synthetic convergence arguments and second-moment measurements do not directly establish held-out generalization. Proposed-method comparisons are excluded under the stated rule. Table uncertainties are reported margins of error; their statistical definition is not supplied. The paper reports broader tuning than the record's framing suggests, and its CIFAR-10 prose and Table 2 disagree on run count.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Broader tuning, switching from Adam to SGD, language-model cases where Adam does better, and explicit tests of training-versus-test performance gaps.
Batch-size effects and adaptation of large-batch recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparison with other generalization measures.

relationships.condition: ImageNet ResNet-18: AMSGrad(W) training versus held-out performance

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10 ResNet-18: decoupled weight decay versus L2 for Adam
relationships.reason: Section 7.6 states that decoupled decay improves testing performance (R20–R21), supporting the recovery direction without establishing parity with SGD.
